summary_paragraph: A young woman with congenital tracheobronchomalacia and tracheostomy status was admitted for dyspnea, cough, green tracheostomy secretions, odynophagia, and neck pain lasting one week. She had recent hospitalizations for similar symptoms without confirmed infection. Evaluation showed no fever, normal white blood cell count, and a chest X-ray without acute findings. Empiric antibiotics were given in the ED but discontinued due to lack of infection markers. Symptoms were attributed to airway irritation from inconsistent humidification. Pain was managed with opioids, and tracheostomy care was reinforced. She remained stable, symptoms improved, and she was discharged home with updated medications, a limited supply of oxycodone and gabapentin, Plan B for contraceptive backup, and recommendations for genetic testing to confirm beta thalassemia. Follow-up with her primary care provider was advised.
problems: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia originating in the perinatal period
